title: Soweto uprising
summary: On 16 June 1976 Black schoolchildren in Soweto marched against the imposition of Afrikaans as a language of instruction, and police opened fire. Protests spread across South Africa. Africanews reports 176 dead after the shooting and closer to 700 nationwide; SAHO states about 566 schoolchildren were killed. International condemnation followed, including a UN arms embargo within a year.

uncertainty.note: The uprising began on 16 June 1976 and protests continued for months; only the opening day is dated here. Death figures differ by source and counting period.

where.historical_name: Soweto, Black township southwest of Johannesburg, Transvaal Province, South Africa

importance.justification: Student revolt that revived mass resistance to apartheid and increased sanctions pressure; commemorated as Youth Day.

audience_note: Describes police shootings of schoolchildren, including a boy aged 12 or 13. Casualty figures are contested.

sources.title: South Africa marks 50th anniversary of the 1976 student uprising

reviewer_note: Deaths: 176 after police opened fire and closer to 700 as protests spread (Africanews); about 566 schoolchildren killed during the protests (SAHO). Hector Pieterson is 12 per SAHO and 13 per Africanews. Pin is the township centre, not a single street.

beats.caption: Students in Soweto protested the use of Afrikaans as a language of instruction; police opened fire.
Condemnation of the police action grew; within a year the UN Security Council imposed an arms embargo on South Africa.
